symptoms: Yellowing and upward curling of upper leaves
Tiny white moth-like flies fluttering when foliage is shaken
Sticky shiny honeydew secretion on leaf surface
Black sooty mold (سیاہ الی) covering foliage and reducing photosynthesis
Stunted plant growth and reduced boll formation
symptoms_ur: پتوں کا اوپر کی طرف مڑنا اور زرد پڑنا
پودا ہلانے پر سفید رنگ کی چھوٹی مکھیاں اڑنا
پتوں کی نچلی سطح پر چپچپا لیس دار مادہ (ہنی ڈیو)
پتوں پر کالی پھپھوند (سیاہ الی) جم جانا
پودے کا قد رک جانا اور ٹینڈے کم بننا
risk_factors: Hot and dry weather followed by intermittent humid spells (30-38°C)
Excessive nitrogenous fertilizer applications
Presence of alternate weed hosts (Itsit, Peeli Buti, Kanghi Buti)
Dense plant population with poor air circulation
non_chemical_management: Install yellow sticky traps (10-12 traps per acre) at canopy level for monitoring and trapping
Spray 5% neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) or neem oil at early pest appearance
Eradicate broadleaf weed hosts around water channels and field borders
Conserve natural predators such as ladybird beetles, lacewings (Chrysoperla), and Geocoris bugs
Avoid early-season broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroids which flare up whitefly populations

verified_treatment.spray_timing: Early morning or late afternoon with hollow cone nozzle
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Ensure complete spray coverage on the underside of leaves where nymphs and adults congregate. Alternate chemical classes to prevent resistance.
verified_treatment.source: Directorate General of Agriculture Extension & Adaptive Research Punjab (Pest Warning Wing)

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 14 days before cotton picking.
Wear full personal protective equipment (PPE): chemical-resistant gloves, face mask, and eye goggles.
Highly toxic to bees and aquatic organisms; do not spray when honeybees are actively foraging or near water channels.

symptoms: Rosetted flowers (گلاب جیسا پھول) that fail to open normally
Tiny pinhead entry holes on young bolls with no exit frass initially
Premature opening of defective bolls (کھلے ادھورے ٹینڈے)
Damaged and stained cotton lint with eaten seeds inside bolls
Presence of small pinkish caterpillars inside dissected green bolls
symptoms_ur: پھول کا گلاب کی طرح بند رہنا (روزیٹڈ پھول)
نرم ٹینڈوں پر سوئی کے ناکے جتنے باریک سوراخ
ٹینڈوں کا قبل از وقت بد وضع کھلنا
ٹینڈے کے اندر روئی کا خراب ہونا اور بیج کھایا جانا
ٹینڈے توڑنے پر اندر گلابی رنگ کی سنڈی کی موجودگی
risk_factors: Late-sown or prolonged cotton ratoon crops
Unshredded cotton sticks stored in heaps near fields
High humidity and moderate warm temperatures (28-34°C)
Monoculture cotton without crop rotation
non_chemical_management: Install PB-Rope L or sex pheromone Delta traps (5-8 traps/acre) 45 days after sowing
Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis cards (2-3 cards/acre weekly during flowering)
Shred and bury cotton stubbles after harvest; never store unchopped sticks near fields
Avoid planting unauthorized or unapproved seed varieties lacking verified bollworm protection

verified_treatment.spray_timing: At 5% economic threshold level (ETL) of infested bolls/flowers in evening hours
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Direct spray nozzles towards squares, flowers, and developing bolls. Rotate chemistry with Triazophos or Emamectin benzoate.
verified_treatment.source: Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI) Multan & Punjab Pest Warning

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 21 days.
Do not allow livestock or farm animals to graze on sprayed field stalks.
Thoroughly clean sprayer nozzles and discard rinse water away from domestic wells.

pest_name: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus - CLCuV (کپاس کا پتا مروڑ وائرس)
symptoms: Upward or downward leaf cupping and curling
Thickening and darkening of leaf veins (رگوں کا موٹا ہونا)
Enations: small leaf-like outgrowths on the underside of major veins
Severely stunted internodes, bushy growth, and drop of squares/bolls
symptoms_ur: پتوں کے کناروں کا اوپر یا نیچے کی طرف مڑ جانا
پتوں کی رگوں کا موٹا، ابھرا ہوا اور گہرا سبز ہو جانا
پتے کی نچلی سطح پر چھوٹا پتہ نما ابھار (اینیشن) بننا
پودے کا قد چھوٹا رہ جانا اور پھل گودا گر جانا
risk_factors: High whitefly vector population in early vegetative stages (May to July)
Cultivation of susceptible non-certified varieties
Presence of weed hosts (Solanum nigrum, Parthenium, Convolvulus)
non_chemical_management: Sow certified tolerant varieties recommended by Punjab Agriculture Dept (e.g., CIM-663, IUB-2013, MNH-1020)
Rogue out and bury virus-infected plants during first 30-40 days of growth
Maintain optimal balanced nutrition with Zinc sulphate (5 kg/acre) and Boron (300 g/acre) to build plant vigor
Keep field borders clean of perennial solanaceous weeds

verified_treatment.active_ingredient: Vector control: Pyriproxyfen 10.8 EC + Acetamiprid 20 SP
verified_treatment.safe_dosage_per_acre: 250 ml Pyriproxyfen + 125 g Acetamiprid per acre
verified_treatment.spray_timing: Immediately upon spotting whitefly vector before virus spread
verified_treatment.application_instructions: CLCuV is a virus; chemical sprays cannot cure viral infection directly. Sprays must target the whitefly insect vector to prevent transmission.
verified_treatment.source: Cotton Research Station Multan & PARC Entomology Division

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 14 days.
Never spray antibiotics or fungicides for viral diseases; they are completely ineffective.
Wear protective apron and face shield during vector pesticide preparation.

symptoms: Downward curling of leaf margins (اندر کی طرف مڑے ہوئے پتے)
Yellowing followed by reddish-brown marginal necrosis ('hopper burn')
Tiny pale green wedge-shaped insects moving sideways rapidly on leaf underside
Crinkled, brittle, and dry leaves in heavy infestation
symptoms_ur: پتوں کے کناروں کا نیچے کی طرف مڑنا
پتوں کے کناروں کا زرد اور پھر سرخ بھورا ہو کر جل جانا (ہوپر برن)
پتے کی نچلی طرف ترچھے چلنے والے باریک سبز کیڑے
پتوں کا سوکھ کر پاپڑ بن جانا
risk_factors: Humid, cloudy weather and monsoon spells (July - September)
Dense canopy with poor drainage
Varieties with glabrous (hairless) leaf surfaces
non_chemical_management: Select hairy (pubescent) cotton cultivars which deter jassid feeding
Avoid excessive irrigation causing high micro-climate humidity
Spray 5% neem extract or encourage natural predators like geocoris and spiders
Apply balanced potassium fertilizer (SOP) to reinforce leaf cell walls

verified_treatment.spray_timing: When economic threshold of 1-2 jassids per leaf is reached
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Spray with fine mist ensuring coverage of middle and lower canopy leaves where jassids feed.
verified_treatment.source: Punjab Pest Warning & Quality Control of Pesticides

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 14 days.
Do not combine with strongly alkaline foliar fertilizers.
Wear gloves and keep children/animals away from sprayed fields.

pest_name: Stripe Rust / Yellow Rust (گندم کی زرد کنگی)
symptoms: Bright yellow to orange-yellow powdery pustules arranged in parallel linear stripes along leaf veins
Yellow powder staining fingers and clothing when walking through the field
Drying and chlorosis of infected leaves starting from lower to flag leaf
Shrivelled grains and poor ear emergence in severe attacks
symptoms_ur: پتوں پر زرد رنگ کی دھاریاں جن میں ہلدی جیسا پاؤڈر بھرا ہوتا ہے
کھیت میں چلنے پر کپڑوں یا انگلیوں پر پیلا پاؤڈر لگ جانا
پتوں کا زرد ہو کر سوکھنا، خاص طور پر جھنڈے والے پتے (فلیگ لیف) کا متاثر ہونا
سٹوں میں دانے کا سکڑ جانا اور پیداوار میں شدید کمی
risk_factors: Cool temperatures (10-18°C) with persistent fog, high humidity, or dew
Overcast and rainy days during January - March in Punjab and KPK
Susceptible obsolete wheat varieties (e.g., Sehar-06, Faisalabad-08)
Over-application of urea and late sowing
non_chemical_management: Cultivate officially certified rust-resistant wheat varieties (e.g., Akbar-19, Dilkash-20, Subhani-21, Ghazi-19, Fakhar-e-Bhakkar)
Complete sowing within optimal window (November 1 to November 25)
Avoid excessive late nitrogen fertilization; ensure balanced potash (SOP) application
Survey fields weekly during January and February for early yellow foci ('hotspots')

verified_treatment.spray_timing: At first appearance of localized yellow pustules on leaves before widespread infection
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Ensure uniform spray mist on both upper and lower leaf surfaces. Repeat after 14 days only if severe cool-wet weather persists.
verified_treatment.source: Wheat Research Institute Faisalabad & PARC Rust Surveillance Program

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 30 days before wheat harvesting.
Do not graze milch cattle or sheep on treated green wheat fodder for at least 15 days.
Wear protective mask and rubber gloves; avoid spraying against the wind.

pest_name: Wheat Aphid / Chepa (گندم کا سست تیلا)
symptoms: Colonies of tiny green or black wingless insects clustered on wheat stems, ears, and flag leaves
Sticky honeydew causing black sooty mold on developing wheat ears
Premature yellowing of leaves and reduced grain weight (shrivelled kernels)
Weakened tillers during grain filling stage (February - March)
symptoms_ur: سٹوں اور پتوں پر ہرے اور کالے رنگ کے ننھے کیڑوں کا جمگھٹا
سٹوں پر چپچپا لیس دار مادہ اور کالی پھپھوند کا جمنا
دانوں کا چھوٹا اور پچکا رہ جانا
فروری اور مارچ میں پودوں کا قبل از وقت پیلا پڑ جانا
risk_factors: Dry, cloudy, and warm weather during February and March
High doses of nitrogenous fertilizers producing lush succulent growth
Absence or destruction of natural bio-agents like ladybird beetles
non_chemical_management: Conserve ladybird beetles (Coccinella septempunctata), syrphid flies, and chrysoperla predators
Apply light water spray or neem seed extract (5%) on borders to dislodge colonies
Avoid late nitrogen top-dressing after heading stage
Irrigate fields timely; water-stressed wheat is more susceptible to aphid multiplication

verified_treatment.spray_timing: Only when economic threshold of 15-20 aphids per earhead is crossed
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Direct spray towards wheat ears and flag leaves. Use hollow cone nozzles. Do NOT spray if natural predator ladybird beetles are abundant.
verified_treatment.source: Directorate General of Pest Warning & Quality Control of Pesticides Punjab

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 21 days.
Extremely toxic to honeybees. NEVER spray during morning hours when pollinators are active.
Do not feed sprayed wheat straw or green fodder to animals within 21 days.

pest_name: Loose Smut (گندم کا کنگی / کالا سٹا)
category: Fungal Disease (بیج سے پیدا ہونے والی پھپھوندی)
symptoms: Entire wheat earhead converted into a loose black powdery mass of fungal spores
Black powder blowing away in wind, leaving only the bare central rachis (خالی ڈنڈی)
Infected ears emerging earlier than healthy heads
Clean leaves and stems, with disease manifesting only upon ear emergence
symptoms_ur: گندم کا پورا سٹا کوئلے جیسے کالے سفوف میں تبدیل ہو جانا
ہوا چلنے پر کالا پاؤڈر اڑ جانا اور صرف سوکھی ڈنڈی باقی رہ جانا
متاثرہ سٹے صحت مند سٹوں سے پہلے نکل آنا
پودے کے پتے صاف دکھائی دینا مگر سٹا کالا نکلنا
risk_factors: Use of uncertified farmer-saved seeds from previously infected fields
Humid and cloudy weather during flowering stage of the previous crop
Planting untreated seed without systemic fungicide coating
non_chemical_management: Solar seed treatment (سولر طریقہ علاج): Soak seed in water for 4-5 hours on a bright sunny summer day (June), then spread thinly on cloth under hot sun to dry
Procure certified seed from Punjab Seed Corporation (PSC) or registered seed companies
Carefully pull out black smutted ears in a plastic bag before spores disperse and bury them deeply
Do not save seed from a field showing even 1% loose smut infestation

verified_treatment.active_ingredient: Seed Treatment: Difenoconazole 30 FS or Tebuconazole 60 FS
verified_treatment.safe_dosage_per_acre: 2.0 ml per kg of seed (Difenoconazole) or 2.5 g per kg of seed (Homai)
verified_treatment.spray_timing: Pre-sowing seed dressing only; foliar spray in standing crop is totally ineffective
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Mix the recommended fungicide in 1 liter of water per 50 kg seed bag, coat thoroughly so every grain is treated, dry in shade, and sow immediately.
verified_treatment.source: Punjab Seed Corporation & Wheat Research Institute

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): Seed treatment only (Not applicable to foliar).
Treated seed is POISONOUS. Never use treated seed for human consumption, flour milling, or poultry feed.
Wear rubber gloves and dust mask during seed treatment.

pest_name: Rice Blast & Neck Blast (دھان کا جھلساؤ اور گردن توڑ)
symptoms: Diamond or spindle-shaped lesions on leaves with gray-white centers and dark reddish-brown margins
Lesions coalescing causing complete leaf drying and burnt appearance
Neck blast: Blackish necrotic lesion at panicle base causing neck breakage (گردن ٹوٹ جانا)
White, unfilled, erect panicles ('white heads' without grain weight)
symptoms_ur: پتوں پر آنکھ یا تکونی شکل کے دھبے جن کا درمیان سفید سرمئی اور کنارے کتھئی ہوں
دھبوں کا آپس میں مل کر پورے پتے کا جھلس جانا
سٹے کی گردن کالی ہو کر ٹوٹ جانا (گردن توڑ)
سٹوں کا سفید، خالی اور بغیر دانے کے کھڑے رہ جانا
risk_factors: High relative humidity (>90%) with prolonged dew periods and moderate temperatures (20-28°C)
Excessive nitrogen application (heavy urea doses)
Cultivation of susceptible aromatic varieties like Super Basmati under dense spacing
Intermittent drought stress followed by flooding
non_chemical_management: Treat nursery seed before sowing with fungicide
Split nitrogen doses into 3 equal applications; never apply urea late after panicle initiation
Maintain continuous shallow water depth (2-3 inches) in fields to reduce disease severity
Burn or plow down infected stubbles after harvest to destroy overwintering mycelium

verified_treatment.spray_timing: Preventative spray at late boot stage and repeated at 10% panicle emergence
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Ensure thorough coverage of both foliage and panicle neck. Spray during calm morning hours with mist nozzle.
verified_treatment.source: Rice Research Institute Kala Shah Kaku & PARC Rice Program

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 21 days.
Do not drain spray runoff water into fish farms, poultry ponds, or drinking canals.
Wear waterproof boots, apron, and gloves during spraying in paddy water.

pest_name: Rice Stem Borer (دھان کے تنے کی سنڈی)
category: Insect Pest (تنے میں سوراخ کرنے والی سنڈی)
symptoms: Dead heart (ڈیڈ ہارٹ): Central shoot of young tiller dries up and can be easily pulled out
White head (سفید سٹا): Panicles dry, turn completely white, and remain devoid of grain at reproductive stage
Bore holes near water level on stems with yellowish frass inside
Larvae feeding inside the hollow stem causing tiller death
symptoms_ur: ڈیڈ ہارٹ: پودے کی درمیانی کونپل سوکھ جانا اور کھینچنے پر آسانی سے نکل آنا
سفید سٹا: سٹے کا سفید اور خالی نکلنا جس میں دانے نہ بنیں
پودے کے نچلے حصے میں تنے پر سوراخ اور اندر سنڈی کا فضلہ
تنے کو اندر سے کھوکھلا کر دینا
risk_factors: Late transplanting of paddy nursery after July 15
Stubbles left in the field after mechanical harvesting without deep plowing
Continuous cloudy, humid monsoon weather
Stagnant water without drainage
non_chemical_management: Clip the top tips of nursery seedlings before transplanting to remove borer egg masses
Install pheromone traps (4-5 traps/acre) to monitor moth flights and time applications
Plow fields deeply with disc/mouldboard plow immediately after harvest and irrigate to drown hibernating larvae in stubbles
Encourage biological control agents like Trichogramma wasps and spiders in the paddy ecosystem

verified_treatment.spray_timing: Broadcast granular application in standing water 25-30 days and 50 days after transplanting
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Maintain 2-3 inches of standing water in the paddy field for 4-5 days after broadcasting granules to ensure systemic uptake by roots.
verified_treatment.source: Rice Research Institute Punjab & Federal Plant Protection Department

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 28 days.
Extremely hazardous to fish, frogs, and aquatic life. Do not discharge paddy water into natural water bodies.
Wear rubber gloves and boots when broadcasting granular formulations; never handle with bare hands.

pest_name: Bacterial Leaf Blight - BLB (دھان کا بیکٹیریل بلائٹ)
symptoms: Water-soaked yellowish-green stripes on leaf margins starting near leaf tips
Wavy or undulating margins along lesions progressing downwards
Lesions turning grayish-white with milky bacterial ooze beads in early morning
Kresek symptom in young plants: entire seedling wilts, rolls, and dies
symptoms_ur: پتے کے کناروں سے شروع ہونے والی زرد سبزی مائل لہراتی دھاریاں
دھاریوں کا بڑھ کر پتے کا اوپر سے نیچے تک خشک اور سفید ہو جانا
صبح کے وقت پتوں پر بیکٹیریا کے قطرے (اووز) نظر آنا
شدید حملے میں پودے کا سوکھ جانا
risk_factors: Severe storms, rain accompanied by strong winds which create leaf micro-wounds
Deep standing water and high nitrogen fertilizer levels
High temperatures (25-34°C) with 70-85% humidity during monsoon
non_chemical_management: Drain standing water from infected fields for 2-3 days to halt bacterial spread
Immediately withhold further urea or nitrogen top-dressing; apply Muriate of Potash or SOP (15-20 kg/acre)
Avoid handling or working in paddy fields while foliage is wet to prevent mechanical transmission
Select certified BLB-tolerant cultivars like KSK-133 or Basmati-515

verified_treatment.active_ingredient: Copper Hydroxide 77 WP or Bismerthiazol 20 WP
verified_treatment.spray_timing: At initial onset of wavy marginal leaf lesions before whole canopy turns straw-colored
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Ensure clean spray water. Copper bactericides act as protective barriers; repeat spray after 10-12 days if strong rainstorms continue.
verified_treatment.source: Directorate of Rice Research & PARC Crop Diseases Research Institute

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 14 days.
Do not mix copper formulations with organophosphates or acidic chemicals.
Wear protective eyewear to avoid copper dust irritation.

pest_name: Fall Armyworm (مکئی کا فال آرمی ورم)
symptoms: Large ragged irregular holes in maize leaves with extensive sawdust-like frass (گوبر جیسا فضلہ)
Central whorl severely chewed, ragged, and hollowed out
Larvae having an inverted white 'Y' mark on the head capsule and 4 dark spots arranged in a square on the 8th abdominal segment
Damage extending into young developing corn cobs and silk
symptoms_ur: پتوں میں بڑے بے ڈھنگے سوراخ اور لکڑی کے برادے جیسا فضلہ
مکئی کی گوبھ کا اندر سے بری طرح کھایا جانا
سنڈی کے سر پر الٹے 'Y' کا سفید نشان اور دم کے قریب چار کالے نقطے
چھلی کے دانوں اور بالوں کو کھا جانا
risk_factors: Continuous, staggered maize plantings throughout spring, summer, and autumn
Warm temperatures (25-32°C) without heavy rains
Late sown crops adjacent to older infested fields
non_chemical_management: Hand-pick and crush egg masses and young larvae during early crop establishment (first 2-4 weeks)
Apply dry sand or wood ash mixed with chili powder into the central whorl of attacked plants
Install sex pheromone lure traps (5 traps/acre) for monitoring adult moths
Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) formulations (2 g/liter) or Metarhizium anisopliae bio-fungicides

verified_treatment.active_ingredient: Emamectin Benzoate 1.9 EC or Chlorantraniliprole 20 SC
verified_treatment.spray_timing: Early morning or late evening directing spray cone directly into the plant whorl (گوبھ کے اندر)
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Must direct the spray nozzle straight down into the leaf whorl so the chemical penetrates where larvae shelter. Flat fan broadcast spray is ineffective.
verified_treatment.source: CABI Pakistan & Maize and Millets Research Institute (MMRI) Yusafwala

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 14 days for green cobs; 21 days for grain.
Do not feed treated maize plants as green fodder to dairy cattle within 14 days.
Always wear rubber gloves, face mask, and eye goggles.

pest_name: Potato Late Blight (آلو کا پچھیتا جھلساؤ)
symptoms: Water-soaked irregular dark green to blackish lesions on leaves and stems
White cottony or powdery fungal growth on the underside of lesions during humid early mornings
Rapid blighting, blackening, and foul odor of the entire potato foliage within 48-72 hours
Brownish dry rot with granular texture under the skin of infected potato tubers
symptoms_ur: پتوں اور تنوں پر پانی سے بھیگے ہوئے کالے یا گہرے سبز دھبے
صبح سویرے نمی کے وقت پتے کی نچلی سطح پر سفید روئی نما پھپھوند
دو سے تین دن میں پورا کھیت کالا ہو کر جل جانا اور بدبو آنا
آلو کے اندر کتھئی رنگ کا سوکھا سڑاؤ پیدا ہونا
risk_factors: Cold, overcast, foggy weather with temperatures between 10-20°C and relative humidity >85%
Frequent winter rains or heavy night dew in December and January across Punjab potato belt
Dense canopy with poor air movement and flood irrigation
non_chemical_management: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers from reputable sources
Ensure high earthing-up (مٹی چڑھانا) to cover tubers with at least 4-5 inches of soil, preventing spore wash down into tubers
Kill potato haulms (بیلیں کاٹنا / جلانا) 10-14 days prior to harvest to prevent tuber contamination
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; irrigate only in furrows avoiding water logging

verified_treatment.active_ingredient: Dimethomorph 50 WP + Mancozeb 75 WP or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb
verified_treatment.spray_timing: Preventative spray before fog/rain, or immediate curative spray at first lesion sight
verified_treatment.application_instructions: High volume spray (120 liters water/acre) ensuring complete lower leaf coverage. Alternate systemic fungicides (Acrobat/Revus) with contact protectors (Mancozeb).
verified_treatment.source: Potato Research Institute Sahiwal & PARC Plant Pathology Division

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 14 days before digging tubers.
Do not consume or store blighted, rotten tubers.
Wear full protective rubber suit, gloves, and respiratory mask during spraying.

pest_name: Tomato Leaf Miner (ٹماٹر کی سرنگ بنانے والی سنڈی)
category: Insect Pest (پتوں میں سرنگ بنانے والی سنڈی)
symptoms: Irregular blotch-like mines or transparent blisters on tomato leaves (سرنگیں / چھالے)
Black frass (کیڑے کا فضلہ) clearly visible inside the transparent leaf mines
Bore holes near fruit calyx with rotting inside young green tomatoes
Desiccated leaves with severe defoliation and unmarketable fruit
symptoms_ur: پتوں کے اندر شفاف چھالے اور ٹیڑھی میڑھی سرنگیں
سرنگ کے اندر کالا فضلہ صاف دکھائی دینا
ٹماٹر کے پھل کے پاس باریک سوراخ اور اندر سے پھل کا سڑنا
پتوں کا سوکھ کر گرنا اور پیداوار کا ضائع ہونا
risk_factors: Warm greenhouse, tunnel, or open-field conditions (22-30°C)
Continuous solanaceous vegetable cropping without host-free periods
Transport of infested seedling trays across nurseries
non_chemical_management: Install Tuta-specific pheromone water-pan traps or Delta traps (10-15 traps/acre) for mass trapping
Cover nursery tunnels with 40-50 mesh insect-proof netting
Remove and incinerate mined leaves and infested tomato fruits daily
Conserve mirid bugs (Nesidiocoris tenuis) which feed voraciously on Tuta eggs and larvae

verified_treatment.active_ingredient: Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG or Spinetoram 11.7 SC
verified_treatment.spray_timing: At first detection of leaf mines during morning or evening
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Thoroughly drench the entire plant canopy including lower older leaves. Avoid consecutive sprays of the same mode of action.
verified_treatment.source: Vegetable Research Institute Faisalabad & CABI Bio-protection Portal

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 7 days for fresh market tomatoes.
Never spray during tomato fruit picking days. Wait full 7 days after application.
Wear full protective gear (gloves, mask, protective glasses).

pest_name: Chilli Anthracnose / Fruit Rot (مرچ کا پھل گلنا / انتھراکنوز)
symptoms: Sunken circular or oval dark lesions on ripening green and red chilli fruits
Concentric rings of tiny black fungal dots (acervuli) inside the fruit lesions
Premature drop and rotting of affected chillies
Dieback of branches: twigs drying from the top downwards with straw-colored appearance
symptoms_ur: لال اور ہری مرچوں پر اندر کو دھنسے ہوئے گول یا بیضوی کالے دھبے
دھبوں کے اندر دائروں کی شکل میں باریک کالے نقطے
مرچوں کا داغدار ہو کر قبل از وقت گرنا اور سڑنا
شاخوں کا اوپر سے نیچے کی طرف سوکھنا (ڈائی بیک)
risk_factors: High temperatures (28-32°C) combined with high rainfall or heavy sprinkler irrigation
Relative humidity exceeding 80% during fruit maturation
Infected seeds or crop debris from previous chilli crop
non_chemical_management: Use disease-free certified seeds; perform hot water seed treatment (52°C for 30 minutes)
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; use ridge-and-furrow system with good drainage
Harvest ripe fruits promptly; do not allow over-ripe fruits to hang on bushes
Solarize soil and rotate with non-solanaceous crops like maize or pulses for 2 years

verified_treatment.active_ingredient: Azoxystrobin 200 g/l + Difenoconazole 125 g/l or Mancozeb 75 WP
verified_treatment.spray_timing: At flowering and fruit initiation stage before onset of monsoon rains
verified_treatment.application_instructions: Spray thoroughly to cover both leaves and fruit bunches. Repeat after 12-14 days if rainfall and humid weather continue.
verified_treatment.source: Vegetable Research Institute Faisalabad & Sindh Agriculture Research Institute Tandojam

safety_notes: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 10 days for green chillies; 14 days for dry red chillies.
Do not pick chillies within the PHI period.
Wash hands and face with soap after handling fungicide containers.
